title: Lepton mass ratios in $\mathbb{C}[z]$
html:
The archimedean realization (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) assigns mass values to knot configurations. The quantum Planck constant evaluates to

  \hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1}.

At q_0 \approx 1.10998:

  \hbar_{q_0} \approx 0.09908,
  \qquad
  \hbar_{q_0}^{-2} \approx 101.86.

Evaluating over \mathbb{C}[z] at z = q_0 gives the dimensionless lepton mass ratios:

Particle Closure \mathrm{Vol}(K) \mathfrak{m}(K)/m_e
Electron Hopf link, closure of \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 0 (not hyperbolic) 1 (the unit)
Muon figure-eight knot 4_1 2.0299 \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_{q_0}^2 \approx 206.77

Neither row is a prediction. The electron row is the unit, and the muon row is the relation that fixes q_0 through the calibration CAL-2 (three-calibration discipline), so it holds by construction. The proton and neutron are not listed: under the pair Skein formula their masses are an invertible function of two dressed quark masses (nucleon masses under the pair Skein formula), so tabulating them against CODATA would test nothing.

The fibre functor \tau maps the categorical Frobenius form to the Tanaka–Webster inner product. Specializing z \mapsto q_0 recovers the numerical values while preserving the algebraic structure.
